name: Conventional TACE (DOXOrubicin or cisplatin, intra-arterial + embolization)
cyclesNote: Transarterial chemoembolization is delivered on-demand, not on a fixed calendar. Sessions are repeated for viable/residual tumor at roughly 6 to 8 week intervals with response imaging and a liver-function check before each session; the cycle count here is a nominal planning default only. Conventional TACE is a single-agent choice: doxorubicin OR cisplatin emulsified in lipiodol, followed by embolic particles. Both agents are listed so either can be selected; they are not both given in one session by default.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

premedications.name: Antiemetic and analgesic cover
premedications.notes: Peri-procedure antiemetic and analgesia for expected post-embolization symptoms; periprocedural antibiotic prophylaxis per interventional-radiology practice.

supportiveCare: Selective / superselective delivery to spare non-tumor parenchyma and preserve liver reserve.
Anticipate and manage post-embolization syndrome (pain, fever, nausea, transient transaminitis).
Reassess Child-Pugh status before each session; avoid repeat sessions that would compromise liver reserve.
Continue antiviral therapy for viral hepatitis and hepatology co-management.
monitoring: liver function and bilirubin before and after each session
AFP trend and multiphasic CT / MRI response imaging
renal function (contrast and cisplatin nephrotoxicity if cisplatin used)
cumulative anthracycline exposure if doxorubicin used

doseModificationRules.condition: declining liver reserve (rising bilirubin, new ascites, Child-Pugh worsening)
doseModificationRules.text: Do not repeat chemoembolization when liver reserve is declining; reassess for systemic therapy or best supportive care. Physician decides.

doseModificationRules.condition: cumulative intra-arterial DOXOrubicin approaching lifetime anthracycline limits
doseModificationRules.text: Track cumulative anthracycline exposure across all routes; approaching 450 mg/m2 warrants review and 550 mg/m2 is the conventional hard cap for cumulative cardiotoxicity. Physician decides.

drugs.name: DOXOrubicin (intra-arterial)
drugs.notes: Conventional TACE option: DOXOrubicin about 50 mg/m2 (commonly 50 to 75 mg total) emulsified in lipiodol and delivered into the tumor-feeding hepatic artery, followed by embolic particles to stagnation. Single-agent choice (use doxorubicin OR cisplatin, not both). ISMP tall-man. Track cumulative anthracycline exposure for cardiotoxicity. Authored from standard interventional-oncology practice; the operator selects the actual per-session dose by tumor burden and liver reserve.

drugs.name: Cisplatin (intra-arterial)
drugs.notes: Alternative conventional TACE agent: cisplatin (about 100 mg per session, or roughly 2 mg/kg) emulsified in lipiodol and delivered intra-arterially, followed by embolization. Single-agent choice (use cisplatin OR doxorubicin, not both). Ensure adequate hydration and monitor renal function. Authored from standard interventional-oncology practice; the operator sets the actual per-session dose.
